issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the UML in problem_statement.md declares the collection as 'animals: List<Animal>' (problem_statement.md lines 16-18), while the textual Part 3 instructions explicitly require using a Set implemented as a HashSet to enforce uniqueness (problem_statement.md lines 108-111). The provided solution implementation defines the field as 'private List<Animal> animals;' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 9) and the template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-5) contains a TODO and does not implement the collection. This contradiction leaves students unclear whether to implement Farm.animals as a List (allowing duplicates) or a Set/HashSet (preventing duplicates), which affects the addAnimal and iteration behavior and the correctness expectations for the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the collection type for Farm.animals consistent across all materials. Two actionable options:
1) If uniqueness of animals is intended (prevent duplicates): update the UML and any List references to 'Set<Animal>' (or 'HashSet' in implementation notes), change the solution and template to use 'private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();', and adapt addAnimal/feedAllAnimals to work with Set iteration. Update any explanatory text to mention uniqueness.
2) If duplicates are acceptable: remove the Set/HashSet requirement from the textual Part 3 and ensure UML and solution use 'List<Animal>' consistently (and adjust wording about uniqueness). Prefer option 1 if the exercise author intended to enforce uniqueness; otherwise choose option 2 and remove the HashSet requirement from the text.
